Payment Success Ratio — what it is, why it was low, and how we raised it

Every number below is measured on the exact 18,331-node / 80,918-channel paper snapshot. The success ratio is not a free parameter: it is bounded by the liquidity available at the sender and receiver. This page separates the routing fix from the workload fix so neither is mistaken for the other.

METRIC 1

Success ratio

successful payments ÷ attempted payments

Counts a payment only when the full requested amount is delivered. A failed partial delivery counts as zero.

METRIC 2

Success volume

delivered satoshis ÷ attempted satoshis

Weighted by amount. A protocol can have many tiny successes yet a poor volume ratio.

METRIC 3

Liquidity ceiling

max-flow on the initial balances

The most any router can do for that payment. If the sender cannot send it, no algorithm can.

Reproduce this measurement

From the project root; the cached-route file is built once and reused.

python3 scripts/success_experiment.py --output data --workers 6

Outputs: success_experiment.json, success_per_run.csv, success_deciles.csv, success_failures.csv. The snapshot itself is read from the original project folder; every result written here lives in this folder.
